quests.ruleExplanation: In statements the manager is comes before the complement; to ask, is moves in front of the subject: Is the manager available?
quests.nativeTip: With is/are/am, swap the subject and the verb to make a question — the verb moves to the front.

quests.ruleExplanation: Are switches places with the results, moving to the very front of the sentence to signal a yes/no question.
quests.nativeTip: Are works the same way as is: it jumps ahead of the subject to open the question.

quests.ruleExplanation: Is still leads the question even though the subject your presentation includes a possessive word, followed by finished at the end.
quests.nativeTip: A possessive subject doesn't change anything — is still comes first, then the subject, then the description.

quests.sentence: Does she like her new job?
quests.ruleExplanation: Since like is an ordinary verb (not be), the question needs does at the front, followed by she, then the base verb like.
quests.nativeTip: Ordinary verbs need a helper — does goes first, then the subject, then the base form of the verb.

quests.ruleExplanation: They is plural, so do is used instead of does; it still comes first, before the subject and the base verb accept.
quests.nativeTip: With a plural subject, do (not does) leads the question, followed by the base verb.

quests.sentence: Does the printer need more paper?
quests.ruleExplanation: Does opens the sentence before the printer, and need stays in its base form even though the object more paper is longer.
quests.nativeTip: Even with a longer object, does still opens the question, right before the subject.

quests.ruleExplanation: Did signals past tense at the front of the question, so finish returns to its base form instead of finished.
quests.nativeTip: Did replaces does/do for the past, and the main verb goes back to its base form.

quests.ruleExplanation: Did carries the past-tense meaning at the start, which is why cancel appears in its base form rather than cancelled.
quests.nativeTip: The base-form rule still applies: cancel, not cancelled, after the subject.

quests.sentence: Did the delivery arrive on time?
quests.ruleExplanation: Did leads the sentence, the delivery is the subject, and on time (a time expression) simply follows the base verb arrive at the end.
quests.nativeTip: Did still opens the question even when a time phrase follows the verb.

quests.ruleExplanation: Where asks about location and opens the sentence, followed by the same is-before-subject inversion used in yes/no questions.
quests.nativeTip: A question word replaces the missing information and takes the very first position, before the inverted verb.

quests.ruleExplanation: Who replaces the unknown person's name and comes first, with is following it and then the subject your supervisor.
quests.nativeTip: Who asks about a person and still leads the sentence, followed by is and the subject.

quests.ruleExplanation: What opens the question about an unknown item, followed by is, then the subject the correct password.
quests.nativeTip: What asks about a thing and takes the same front position, before is and the subject.

quests.sentence: What time does the store open?
quests.ruleExplanation: What time leads the question, does follows as the helper verb, and open stays in its base form after the subject the store.
quests.nativeTip: The question word comes first, then does, then the subject, then the base verb.

quests.ruleExplanation: Where opens the question, do you follows, and usually keeps its familiar mid-position right before the base verb park.
quests.nativeTip: A frequency word can still appear inside a question, sitting in its usual mid-position before the verb.

quests.ruleExplanation: Why opens the question, does supports the subject she, and avoid stays in base form, with meetings as the object.
quests.nativeTip: Why asks for a reason and leads the sentence, followed by does, the subject, and the base verb.

quests.sentence: Where did you buy that jacket?
quests.ruleExplanation: Where leads the question, did signals past tense, and buy stays in its base form after the subject you, with that jacket as the object.
quests.nativeTip: The question word opens the sentence, then did, then the subject, then the base verb and object.

quests.ruleExplanation: When opens the question, did follows, and depart appears in base form after the subject the flight.
quests.nativeTip: When asks about time and takes the same front position before did and the subject.

quests.ruleExplanation: Why comes first, did follows, and fail remains in base form after the subject the project, just as in the previous two questions.
quests.nativeTip: Why still leads the question, with did carrying the past meaning so the verb stays in its base form.

quests.ruleExplanation: Who is the subject itself here (asking about the caller), so called follows it directly with no do/does/did needed, unlike object questions.
quests.nativeTip: When who or what IS the subject doing the action, no extra helper verb is needed — just who/what, then the verb.

quests.ruleExplanation: What is the subject asking what caused something, so caused follows directly — no auxiliary is inserted before the verb.
quests.nativeTip: What plays the role of subject, so the verb follows immediately in its normal form.

quests.ruleExplanation: Who is the subject and manages keeps the same -s ending it would have in a statement, since no auxiliary is used when who is the subject.
quests.nativeTip: Compare this to WH questions with does — here who is the subject, so manages keeps its subject-verb agreement, with no does needed.

quests.sentence: How can I reset my password?
quests.ruleExplanation: How opens the question, can (a modal) follows, and reset stays in base form after the subject I.
quests.nativeTip: The question word leads, then the modal, then the subject, then the base verb.

quests.sentence: Where should we park the car?
quests.ruleExplanation: Where leads the sentence, should follows as the modal, and park stays in base form after we, with the car as the object.
quests.nativeTip: Where comes first, then the modal should, then the subject, then the base verb and object.

quests.ruleExplanation: What opens the question, should follows as the modal, and prioritize stays in base form after the subject the team.
quests.nativeTip: What leads the question, then the modal could, then the subject, then the base verb.

quests.sentence: Can you send me the file?
quests.ruleExplanation: Can moves to the front, ahead of you, and send stays in base form — modals invert the same way is and are do.
quests.nativeTip: Modals invert with the subject just like be does: modal first, then subject, then base verb.

quests.ruleExplanation: Could opens the sentence before she, and join remains in base form, followed by the object the call.
quests.nativeTip: Could leads the question the same way, with the subject and base verb following in order.

quests.ruleExplanation: Should leads the question before we, and reschedule stays in base form, with the appointment as the object.
quests.nativeTip: Should still comes first, before the subject, with the main verb kept in its base form.

quests.sentence: Why did the shipment arrive late?
quests.ruleExplanation: Why opens the question, did carries the past tense, and arrive stays in base form after the shipment, with late describing how it arrived.
quests.nativeTip: Review the did-pattern: question word, then did, then subject, then base verb, then any extra detail.

quests.sentence: Could you explain the new policy?
quests.ruleExplanation: Could leads the question before you, and explain stays in base form, followed by the new policy as the object.
quests.nativeTip: Review the modal pattern: modal first, then subject, then base verb, then a describing object.

quests.sentence: What time does the training session begin?
quests.ruleExplanation: What time opens the question, does follows as the helper, and begin stays in base form after the subject the training session.
quests.nativeTip: Review the do/does pattern with a compound noun: question word, then does, then subject, then base verb.
